video_caption: The video opens with an animated patriotic theme featuring red, white, and blue stripes and stars. Text transitions onto the screen, first showing "LWV LEAGUE OF WOMEN VOTERS of PORTLAND," followed by an outline of Oregon that changes from blue to red, alongside a "VOTE" button and the word "DEMOCRACY." The background then becomes solid red as a stylized red star with a blue center appears, and a blue banner scrolls in with the text "ELECTION 2020." Further text identifies the segment as a "Video Voters' Guide" for "Candidate Portland City Commissioner Position 2 Julia DeGraw." The scene then cuts to a woman with short blonde hair and glasses, wearing a light green turtleneck and black blazer, speaking directly to the camera from a home interior with plants and framed artwork. She introduces herself as Colleen Shoemaker from the League of Women Voters of Portland. The screen then splits horizontally, showing Colleen on the left and Julia DeGraw, a woman with reddish-brown hair wearing a dark patterned top and a long necklace with earbuds, smiling at Colleen on the right. A banner at the bottom displays "LWV Video Voters' Guide League of Women Voters of Portland lwvpdX.org." Colleen welcomes Julia and invites her to speak, and Julia responds, "Hello. Thanks for having me."

The video opens with a split screen, showing two women in separate video calls. On the left, an older woman with blonde hair and glasses, wearing a light green turtleneck and dark blazer, listens attentively, looking slightly downward. To her left is a plant with red berries in a blue vase, and behind her are framed pictures on a light-colored wall. On the right, a younger woman with dark hair pulled back, wearing a dark blue patterned top and wired earphones, speaks directly to the camera with an animated expression. Behind her, a framed picture of a tree with a bright background hangs on a light-colored wall. At 0:02, the screen zooms in on the speaking woman, and a text overlay appears at the bottom left: "LWV Julia DeGraw Candidate Portland City Commissioner Position 2." (LWV stands for League of Women Voters, indicating the context of the interview, and the text identifies the speaker as Julia DeGraw, a candidate for Portland City Commissioner Position 2).

A woman with light brown hair, pulled back, and light skin is speaking directly to the camera, wearing a dark blue patterned top and a multi-strand necklace, with red wired earbuds visible. She maintains a serious but engaged expression as she talks, her mouth slightly open. The background is a plain light gray wall, with a framed picture to her right showing a bare tree against a glowing light or sunset, possibly with a heart shape. At 0:39, a white box with a blue border appears at the bottom left, displaying the "LWV" logo, and two website addresses, "Vote411.org" and "lwvppdx.org." From 0:54 to 0:56, a loud, high-pitched static sound interrupts the audio, but the woman continues to speak, and the sound abruptly ceases at 0:56.

The video opens with a medium close-up of a woman with auburn hair, tied back, wearing a dark blue patterned top and multiple necklaces, one of which holds red earbuds. She is speaking directly to the camera with an earnest expression, her head moving slightly as she talks. The background is a plain light grey wall with a framed picture of a bare tree with a red heart painted on its trunk. At the 0:05 mark, the screen splits into two vertical frames. The first woman remains on the right side, continuing to speak. On the left side, an older woman with short blonde hair and glasses, wearing a light green turtleneck under a dark jacket, appears. She looks at the camera with a neutral, attentive expression. Her background includes a light-colored wall, framed pictures, and a blue vase with greenery. At 0:16, the screen reverts to the single frame of the first woman, who continues speaking, and a "MetroEast" logo with a stylized green and orange 'm' and 'e' appears in the bottom right corner. The first woman finishes her statement around 0:33, and the screen splits again into two. The second woman then says "Thank you" while looking at the camera.

In a split-screen video, an older woman with light-colored hair, glasses, and wearing a light green turtleneck under a dark blazer is on the left, asking a question while looking directly at the camera. Her background includes a kitchen or dining area with a plant in a blue vase and framed pictures on the wall. On the right, a younger woman with darker hair, wearing a dark blue patterned top, red earbuds, and a beaded necklace, listens attentively and nods slightly. Her background is a plain gray wall with a framed picture of a bare tree. At the 0:27 mark, a graphic overlay appears at the bottom left, stating "LWV Julia DeGraw Candidate Portland City Commissioner Position 2," identifying the woman on the right as a political candidate.

A light-skinned woman with reddish-brown hair, styled in an updo, speaks directly to the camera from 00:05 to 00:43. She wears a dark blue patterned top and a long, multi-strand necklace, with red wired earbuds in her ears. Throughout the segment, she maintains a serious and engaged expression, often gesturing with her right hand. The background consists of a plain light gray wall, with two framed pictures: a dark-framed one partially visible to her right, and a larger one to her left depicting a bare tree silhouetted against a reddish-orange glowing sky, resembling a sunset or sunrise. At 00:22, a blue banner appears at the bottom of the screen, displaying the text: "LWV | Video Voters' Guide | League of Women Voters of Portland lwvdpdx.org".

The video opens with a medium shot of a woman with light brown hair pulled back, wearing a dark blue patterned top and a layered necklace with red earphones around her neck, speaking directly to the camera with a serious and engaged expression. The background is a plain light gray wall with a framed picture of a bare tree glowing red on the right. At the 0:13 mark, the screen splits into two, revealing a second woman on the left side. This woman has short blonde hair, wears glasses, a light green turtleneck, and a black blazer, and is listening attentively. Her background is a living room setting with plants, framed pictures, and wooden furniture. A blue and white logo with the letters "LWV" appears at the bottom left of the screen. The video then returns to the first woman at 0:25, who continues to speak directly to the camera, using hand gestures to emphasize her points, maintaining a serious expression. At 0:44, a blue banner appears at the bottom of the screen with white text that reads "LWV Vote411.org lwvppdx.org". The woman continues speaking until the end of the segment, her expression gradually becoming slightly less intense.

The video segment opens with a medium shot of a woman with light brown hair pulled back, wearing a dark blue patterned top and a multi-strand beaded necklace. She has red earphones with one earpiece in her right ear and is speaking directly to the camera with a serious and engaged expression. The background features a plain light grey wall, with a partially visible dark-framed object on the left and a framed artwork of a bare tree with a reddish-orange glow in its center on the right. At 00:20, the video transitions to a split-screen view. On the left side, an older woman with short, light blonde hair and glasses, wearing a light green turtleneck under a dark blazer, is seen looking towards the right with a serious expression against a background of a light wall with framed pictures and a plant with red berries. On the right side, the first woman continues speaking, now looking towards the left, with the same light grey wall and tree artwork behind her. A logo appears in the bottom right corner of the screen, displaying a stylized "m e" in dark teal and red, connected by a red swoosh, with the word "MetroEast" in dark teal written below it.

The video features two women in a split-screen video call format. The woman on the left has short blonde hair, wears glasses, a light green turtleneck, and a dark jacket, and is seated indoors with a plant and framed pictures in the background. The woman on the right has her hair pulled back, wears a dark top with a light pattern, multiple necklaces, and wired earphones; she is seated in front of a plain wall with a framed picture of a tree with a bright center hanging behind her. Both women are speaking and listening, looking towards the camera. From 0:01 to 0:14, a "MetroEast" logo is visible in the bottom right corner. From 0:14 to 0:55, a banner appears in the bottom left corner that reads "LWV Julia DeGraw Candidate Portland City Commissioner Position 2". From 0:55 to the end of the segment, the "MetroEast" logo reappears in the bottom right.

The video segment opens with a split screen featuring two women: on the left, a woman with blonde hair and glasses, wearing a light green turtleneck and black blazer, is speaking and gesturing with her hands, against a background of a light wall with framed pictures and a blue vase with red berries. On the right, a woman with brown hair tied in a bun, wearing a dark blue patterned top, long beaded necklaces, and red wired earphones, is listening attentively, with a slight smile, against a light-colored wall featuring a framed picture of a bare tree with a red heart. At the 0:13 mark, the view transitions to a full-screen shot of the woman from the right. She is now speaking directly to the camera, occasionally making small hand gestures, her expression serious and engaged. A lower third graphic appears at the bottom left of the screen, displaying "LWV Julia DeGraw Candidate Portland City Commissioner Position 2," identifying her and her political candidacy. The background remains the same light wall with the tree picture.

A woman with light brown hair pulled back and light eyes is shown from the chest up, speaking directly to the camera with a focused and serious expression. She is wearing a dark blue patterned top, a multi-strand necklace, and red earbuds with a microphone. The background is a plain light gray wall, featuring a dark-framed picture on the left and a framed artwork of a tree with a red/orange glow at its base on the right. From 0:05 to 0:38, a blue banner with red and white stripes is overlaid at the bottom of the screen, displaying a white "LWV" logo and the text "Video Voters' Guide League of Women Voters of Portland lwvdpdx.org". This banner fades out, and from 0:38 to 0:42, an abstract green and orange "Me" logo with the text "MetroEast" appears in the bottom right corner of the screen.

The video opens with a medium close-up of a woman with light brown hair pulled back, wearing a dark blue patterned top and a long, layered necklace with red wired earbuds, speaking directly to the camera with a serious expression. Behind her is a light gray wall with a framed picture of a bare tree with a glowing red heart on its trunk. At 0:18, the screen transitions to a split view. The woman in the dark blue top is now on the right side, smiling and gesturing with her hands. On the left side, another woman with short blonde hair, wearing glasses, a light green turtleneck, and a dark blazer, appears, smiling and looking towards the woman on the right. Her background includes a potted plant in a blue vase, framed pictures, and a light-colored wall. A blue and white logo "LWV" is visible in the bottom left corner of the left screen.

The video opens with a split screen featuring two women engaged in a video call. On the left, a woman with short blonde hair, glasses, and a light green turtleneck under a black blazer speaks and gestures slightly, while on the right, another woman with long dark hair, a dark patterned top, and a long necklace listens attentively with a neutral expression. The background for the left woman includes a plant with red berries in a blue vase and framed pictures on a wall, while the right woman has a single framed tree picture behind her. The video then zooms in on the speaking woman, who continues to address the viewer with an encouraging expression. Overlaid text appears at the bottom of the screen, displaying "LWW Vote411.org lwvpdx.org," (These are websites for the League of Women Voters of Portland, offering voter information.) before transitioning to a blue screen with a vertical border of white stars on the left. Text in white reads, "League of Women Voters of Portland Presents The Video Voters' Guide" followed by "For more voter information: LWW Vote411.org lwvpdx.org." This text then changes to "Don't forget to cast your ballot! Primary Election May 19th." with the voter information links remaining. Next, the text transitions to a list of acknowledgements: "Thanks to the.. Multnomah Bar Foundation Carol & Velma Saling Foundation Vernier Software & Technology The Wyss Foundation ..for their generous support." The final blue screen displays "Produced by" above a green and orange "me" logo with "MetroEast.org" below it, and "Licensed through: Creative Commons 2020," followed by a brief fade to black. Throughout the blue screen segments, a cheerful, patriotic-sounding instrumental music plays.
